Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:1.english: Members of a group - [This] does not refer to the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:2.hebrew: בני חבורה - שמש המשמש בסעודתן, נכנסין בשלשה להסב, ואם בא יחיד או שנים והסבו, אין על השמש לשמש עלייהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:2.english: Members of a group - [Regarding] a waiter who serves at their meal: they enter with three [members] to recline [for the meal], and if an individual or two came and reclined, it is not [incumbent] upon the waiter to serve them.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:3.hebrew: ויוצאין באחד אחד - כל מי שסיים אכילתו קודם, אם בא לצאת יצא, ואע"פ שקשה לשמש לשרת היחידים הנשארין:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:3.english: And they may leave one by one - Whoever finished his meal first, if he comes to leave, he may leave, even though it is difficult for the waiter to serve the individuals who remain.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:4.hebrew: והוא דעיילי בעידנא דעיילי אינשי - שאין האחרון מאריך יותר משעת סעודת האחרים, וגם בכניסתן לא ימהרו להסב כדי לאחר השמש עד זמן גמר שעת סעודה:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:4.english: And provided that they enter at the time when people enter - That the last one does not prolong [his meal] beyond the mealtime of the others; and also upon their entry, they should not hurry to recline so as to delay the waiter until the end of the mealtime.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:5.hebrew: והא דרגש בהו דיילא - שהודיעו לשמש שזה דרכן לצאת אחד אחד, לפי שטורח הוא לו לשמש היחידים:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:11:5.english: And that [is] when the waiter knew about them - [Meaning] that they informed the attendant that this is their custom, to leave one by one, because it is a burden for him to serve individuals.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:12:1.english: And the last [one] must add money - to the waiter.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:1:1.english: One might [think] it may be - [that] the Paschal offering itself [is] eaten in two groups.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:1:2.hebrew: ת"ל בבית אחד יאכל - וקסבר יש אם למקרא, יאכל אפסח קאי ולא אגברי, כלומר, עיקר תחלת אכילתו תהא בחבורה אחת, ולא יתחלק לשתי חבורות, אבל גברא אי בעי קאי מהכא ואזיל ואכיל הכא, דלא קפיד רחמנא אלא אעיקר תחלת אכילה, מדקרינן יאכל הפסח ולא יאכל אגברא. ואני שמעתי חילוף: ר' יהודה סבר יש אם למקרא — בבית אחד ולא בשני מקומות, ור"ש סבר יש אם למסורת שמסר אונקלוס הגר — בחבורה חדא יתאכל, אבל אשני מקומות לא קפיד. וקשה לי לאומרו, דלא שמעתי מסורת כזה מעולם, ועוד דקיימא לן דר' שמעון יש אם למקרא ס"ל בשמעתא קמייתא דסנהדרין, ועוד לישנא דברייתא דייקא כוותי, דגבי חבורות נקט פסח נאכל ולא נקט שתי חבורות אוכלין אותו, וגבי מקומות נקט האוכל אוכל ולא נקט פסח נאכל. הלכך, כי דרשינן בבית אחד יאכל במקרא אפסח, משמע למעוטי חבורות, וכי דרשינן יאכל אגברי, משמע למעוטי מקומות:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:1:2.english: Therefore, the verse states: "In one house shall it be eaten" - And [Rabbi Shimon] holds that the vocalized text is authoritative: ye'akhel ["shall it be eaten"] refers to the Paschal lamb and not to the people [eating it]. That is to say, the essential beginning of its eating must be in one group, and it shall not be divided into two groups; however, a person, if he wishes, may get up from here and go and eat there, for the Merciful One is particular only about the essential beginning of the eating [being in one group], since we read ye'akhel [referring to] the Paschal lamb, and not yokhal [referring] to the person. And I have heard the opposite [interpretation]: Rabbi Yehudah holds that the vocalized text is authoritative — "in one house" and not in two places; and Rabbi Shimon holds that the tradition [masoret] that Onkelos the Convert transmitted is authoritative — "in one group shall it be eaten," but he is not particular about two places. But it is difficult for me to say it, for I have never heard of such a masoret; and furthermore, it is established for us that Rabbi Shimon holds that the vocalized text is authoritative in the first discussion of Sanhedrin; and furthermore, the wording of the Baraita is precise according to my [view], for regarding groups it states "the Paschal lamb is eaten" and does not state "two groups eat it," and regarding places it states "the one who eats, eats" and does not state "the Paschal lamb is eaten." Therefore, when we expound "in one house shall it be eaten" according to the vocalized reading [ye'akhel] as referring to the Paschal lamb, it implies the exclusion of [multiple] groups; and when we expound [the consonantal reading] yokhal as referring to the people [eating it], it implies the exclusion of [multiple] places.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:3:1.hebrew: ונפרסה מחיצה ביניהן גרסינן - היו יושבין חבורה אחת ואוכלין פסח אחד, ונפרסה מחיצה ביניהן ועשאום שני חבורות — לדברי האומר פסח נאכל בשתי חבורות, גומרין אכילתן. ואע"ג דמאן דאית ליה פסח נאכל בשתי חבורות אוסר לאדם לאכול בשני מקומות, הכא לא נעשה לכל חבורה וחבורה מקומם כמקום אחר, שהרי אינו רואה אויר שלא ראה עד עכשיו, ואין כאן מקום חדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:3:1.english: We read: "And a partition was spread between them" - [They] were sitting [as] one group and eating one Paschal lamb, and a partition was spread between them and made them [into] two groups — according to the one who says a Paschal lamb may be eaten in two groups, they may finish eating it. And even though the one who holds [that] a Paschal lamb may be eaten in two groups forbids a person to eat in two places, here the place of each group does not become like another place, because one does not see any space that one did not see until now, and there is no new place here.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:3:2.hebrew: היו יושבין - ב' חבורות בשני בתים, ואכלו שם פסחיהם, ונסתלקה המחיצה, יש כאן אויר חדש ונעשה לכל חבורה כמקום אחר, והוי ליה כאוכלים במקום הראשון ובשני. הלכך, לדברי האומר אין האוכל אוכל בשני מקומות, אין אוכלים:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:3:2.english: They were sitting - [That is,] two groups in two houses, and they ate their Paschal lambs there, and the partition was removed: there is new airspace here, and it becomes like another place for each group, and it is [considered] as though they are eating in the first place and in the second. Therefore, according to the one who says [that] one who eats may not eat in two places, they may not eat.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:5:1.hebrew: פשיט ליה מפשט - אומרה לשמועה זו פשוטה ומפורשת כמו שאמרנו, שעשיית מחיצה עושה אותן שתי חבורות, וסילוק מחיצה עושה אותן שני מקומות, ולא מספקא ליה בה מידי:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:5:1.english: [He] stated it simply - [He] stated this teaching as simple and explicit, as we have said: that erecting a partition makes them two [separate] groups, and removing a partition makes them two [separate] locations, and he has no doubt about it whatsoever.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:6:1.hebrew: מ"ט - למה לה להפוך פניה, ומאי אורחה בהכי:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:6:1.english: What is the reason - Why should she turn her face, and what is her custom in this?

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:6:2.english: Because she is embarrassed - to eat in front of the people because they are looking at her.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:7:1.hebrew: יתיב - ומטה מקום הסב חשובין היא, והקטנים יושבין על גבי ספסלין, ונוהג עצמו בחשיבות:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:7:1.english: He sat - And a bed is the reclining place of important people, while lesser [people] sit on benches, and [thus] he conducted himself with importance.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:7:2.english: He accepted it the first time - And he did not refuse until they pressed him.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:7:3.english: And he drank it in two [sips] - He paused in [drinking] it.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:7:4.hebrew: ולא אהדר אפיה - לצד אחר, אלא שתה לעיניהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:7:4.english: And he did not turn his face - to another side, rather he drank before their eyes.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:8:1.english: I am the bearer of the name - From my youth, they call me thus: Rav Huna.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:8:2.hebrew: מ"ט כי אמרי לך תיב אפוריא איתיבת - ולא ישבת על גבי קרקע ולא על גבי ספסל, ולהכי בעו ליה, שלא היה מנהגם כך ותמיהא להו:
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:8:2.english: What is the reason [that] when they said to you, "Sit on the bed," you sat - and did not sit on the ground or on a bench? And for this reason they asked him, because it was not their custom [to do] so, and it was surprising to them.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:8:3.hebrew: כל מה שיאמר לך בעל הבית עשה - מתניתא היא במסכת דרך ארץ (בפרק בן עזאי) (ד"א רבה פ"ה):
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:8:3.english: Anything the master of the house says to you, do - It is a baraita in Tractate Derekh Eretz (in the chapter [entitled] Ben Azzai) (Derekh Eretz Rabbah, ch. 5).

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:9:1.english: One may refuse a lesser person - [Refusing] to accept his words until he urges him.

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:9:2.hebrew: ואין מסרבין לגדול - שכן במלאכים שאמרו לאברהם כן תעשה (בראשית יח) ולא סירבו בו, וללוט אמרו כי ברחוב נלין, עד ויפצר בם מאד (שם יט):
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:9:2.english: And one may not refuse a great person - For so [we find] with the angels, who said to Abraham, "So do" (Genesis 18), and did not refuse him; whereas to Lot they said, "For we will lodge in the street," until "and he urged them greatly" (ibid. 19).

Rashi on Pesachim 86b:9:3.hebrew: כלה הופכת פניה תנן - ואין דרך האיש להפוך פניו: רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי כריסו רחבה הואי, כדאמרינן בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף פד.):
Rashi on Pesachim 86b:9:3.english: We learned: A bride turns her face - And it is not the way of a man to turn his face. Rabbi Yishmael bar Rabbi Yosei had a large belly, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaSokher et HaPoalim (Bava Metzia 84a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 86b:11:1.hebrew: נכנסין בג' כו' - פירש ר"ח: חבורה שנמנו על הפסח, ובאו מקצת מהן בעת שדרך בני אדם לאכול, ושגרו הדיילא, פי' שמש, לחפש אחריהם ולא מצאן — אם נתקבצו רק שלשה, אוכלין את הפסח ואין עליהן להמתין עד שיבואו כולם, אבל פחות משלשה — לא. אבל אם היו מקובצים יחד ויצאו ונתאחרו, והדר בהו דיילא ולא מצאן — אפילו לא נשאר רק אחד מהם, אין צריך להמתין, כיון שהיו שם ויצאו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 86b:11:1.english: "They enter with three," etc. - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [Regarding] a group who registered for the Paschal offering, and some of them arrived at the time when people normally eat, and they sent the dayyala — meaning, the attendant — to search for them and he did not find them: if only three have gathered, they may eat the Paschal offering and they do not have to wait until all of them arrive; however, [if there are] fewer than three, [they may] not. But if they were [already] gathered together, and [some] left and were delayed, and the attendant went after them and did not find them — even if only one of them remained, he does not need to wait, since they had [already] been there and left.

Tosafot on Pesachim 86b:12:1.hebrew: אמר רבינא ונותן דמים - האוכל פסח, ולית הלכתא כוותיה. והנ"מ דעל בעידנא דעיילי אינשי, והדר בהו דיילא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 86b:12:1.english: Ravina said: And he gives money - [Meaning] the one who eats the Pesach [offering]. And the halakha is not in accordance with him. And this applies only when he entered at the time when people [normally] enter, and the waiter attended to them.

Tosafot on Pesachim 86b:2:1.hebrew: ומר סבר יש אם למקרא - וא"ת: והא שמעינן ליה לרבי שמעון בפ"ק דקדושין (דף יח:) דאית ליה יש אם למקרא ולמסורת, דדריש "בבגדו בה", "בבוגדו בה", דאין אדם מוכר את בתו לשפחות אחר אישות ולא לאישות אחר שפחות? י"ל: דהתם לא סתרי אהדדי ויכול לדרוש שניהם; אבל הכא, דליכא למידרש אלא חד, דריש מקרא, וכן בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ד.). והא דאמר לעיל (פסחים דף פה.): "המוציא בשר פסח מחבורה לחבורה הרי הוא בלא תעשה", אתי אפילו למאן דאמר פסח נאכל בשתי חבורות, דאחר שנחלק ולקחו כל חבורה חלקה — אסור להוציא חלק חבורה זו לחבורה אחרת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 86b:2:1.english: And the other [i.e., Rabbi Shimon] holds that the vocalized text is authoritative - And if you ask: But have we not heard regarding Rabbi Shimon in the first chapter of Kiddushin (18b) that he holds both the vocalized text and the consonantal text are authoritative, for he expounds "bevigdo bah" [and] "bevogdo bah" [to teach] that a man may not sell his daughter into maidservancy after marriage, nor into marriage after maidservancy? One can answer: There, they do not contradict each other, and he can expound both of them; but here, where it is only possible to expound one, he expounds the vocalized text, and likewise in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (4a). And [as for] that which [the Gemara] stated above (Pesachim 85a): "One who takes out meat of the Paschal offering from one group to another violates a negative commandment," [that] accords even with the one who says that a Paschal offering may be eaten by two groups, for after it has been divided and each group has taken its portion, it is forbidden to take out the portion of this group to another group.

Tosafot on Pesachim 86b:9:1.hebrew: אין מסרבין לגדול - אמאי דיתיב אפוריא, לא שייך למימר משום דאין מסרבין; דישיבת פוריא דבר גסות ושררה הוא, ולא היה לו לישב אי לאו משום "כל מה שיאמר בעל הבית עשה":
Tosafot on Pesachim 86b:9:1.english: One may not refuse a great person - Regarding [the earlier question of] why he sat on the couch, it does not apply to say [that he did so] because "one does not refuse [a great person]"; for sitting on a couch is a matter of arrogance and authority, and he would not have sat were it not for [the principle,] "Whatever the host says, do."
